newsitem.title: USA: U.S. upbeat on anti-terror moves.
newsitem.headline: U.S. upbeat on anti-terror moves.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian officials have agreed on a procedure for restoring security cooperation and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright is encouraged, the State Department said on Tuesday.

During three days of talks with U.S. envoy Dennis Ross, the two sides determined a means of sharing information and acting together to combat terrorism, spokesman James Rubin said, adding: "Now we're going to be looking for results, results, results."

U.S. officials said the two sides, mutually mistrustful after a July 30 suicide bombing in Jerusalem and Israeli actions deplored by Palestinians, had agreed to have intelligence and security experts meet regularly to trade information on extremists and potential attacks.
"And so, this is not a breakthrough. But it is encouraging that a mechanism has been found, and now we're going to look for results, results, results," Rubin told a news briefing.
He said Ross would hold another round of talks in Israel on Wednesday and then fly home to Washington.

No date has been set yet for a trip to the region by Albright, he said. But "to the extent that the discussions over the last 24 hours that we hope to continue today yield results, the trip becomes highly likely," he said.
